sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The Electronic Intifada (EI) is an online publication covering the Israeli–Palestinian conflict from a Palestinian perspective.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: It is published by the nonprofit organization the Middle East Cultural and Charitable Society, which is based in Chicago.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: EI was founded in February 2001 by Ali Abunimah, Arjan El Fassed, Laurie King, and Nigel Parry.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: In April 2008, The Electronic Intifada published an article containing e-mails exchanged by members of the Committee for Accuracy in Middle East Reporting in America (CAMERA).

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: The stated purpose of the group was "help[ing] us keep Israel-related entries on Wikipedia from becoming tainted by anti-Israel editors".

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Five Wikipedia editors involved in a CAMERA campaign were sanctioned by Wikipedia administrators, who wrote that the project's open nature "is fundamentally incompatible with the creation of a private group to surreptitiously coordinate editing by ideologically like-minded individuals".

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: After Al Jazeera decided not to publish The Lobby, its documentary about the pro-Israel political lobby in the US, The Electronic Intifada published a leaked version online in 2018.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: In 2010, the Jerusalem-based pro-Israel organization NGO Monitor criticized the Dutch Interchurch Organisation for Development Cooperation (ICCO) for providing financial support to The Electronic Intifada, which it said was antisemitic and compared Israeli policies with those of the Nazi regime.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: Gerald M. Steinberg, head of the organization, described The Electronic Intifada as "an explicitly pro-Palestinian political and ideological Web site" that hosts "anti-Israel propaganda."

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: Marinus Verweij, chairman of ICCO's executive board said "The EI reports frequently about the violations of human rights and international humanitarian law by the State of Israel.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: In no way is the EI anti-Israel or anti-Semitic."

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: He described The Electronic Intifada as "an important source of information from the occupied Palestinian territories" frequently used by newspapers such as The Washington Post and the Financial Times.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: Dutch Foreign Ministry spokesman Ward Bezemer stated that whether ICCO had promoted antisemitism, a criminal offence, is to be determined by the Public Prosecutor on the basis of Dutch law.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: On 26 November 2010, Dutch Foreign Minister Uri Rosenthal, who is Jewish and has an Israeli wife, said: "I will look into the matter personally.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: If it appears that the government subsidized NGO ICCO does fund The Electronic Intifada, it will have a serious problem with me."

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: Rosenthal later told IKON radio that "anti-semitism is not the issue" but "my concern about calls to contribute to boycotts and embargoes".

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: EI co-founder MP Arjan El-Fassed, who also wrote for the website Al-Awda, told the Dutch newspaper De Volkskrant that the complaint by NGO Monitor was related to one quote from an interview with Jewish Holocaust survivor and anti-Zionist Hajo Meyer in June 2009.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: Meyer told EI: "I can write up an endless list of similarities between Nazi Germany and Israel."

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: In the same article, the Director of the Centre for Information and Documentation Israel (CIDI), Ronnie Naftaniel, said that The Electronic Intifada is not an antisemitic website.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: He stated that, while everybody should be free to express their opinion, the Dutch government should not indirectly fund a website that regularly calls for a boycott of Israel.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: On 14 January 2011, ICCO decided not to change its policy after a discussion held with the Dutch foreign minister.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: In response to ICCO's decision, The Jerusalem Post reported that Dutch Foreign Minister Uri Rosenthal "will monitor ICCO's activities.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: He will consider this as a minus when he makes up the balance when ICCO applies again in a new subsidies round," as said by Ward Bezemer, a spokesman for Rosenthal."

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: Partos, a national umbrella for more than a hundred Dutch civil society organizations in the international development cooperation sector, strongly condemned Rosenthal's threats to ICCO's funding.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: "Rosenthal's position vis-à-vis ICCO creates a dangerous precedent for the future.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: Development organisations will have to continue to fight for an independent voice in the debate.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: Partos will ... stand up for that."

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: In April 2011, Professor of International Cooperation Studies Paul Hoebink argued that Foreign Minister Uri Rosenthal has no say in Dutch government funding to ICCO because Minister Ben Knapen holds the portfolio.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: In addition, ICCO's contribution to The Electronic Intifada is paid with ICCO's own funds.

sentences.section: Conflict with NGO Monitor over Dutch funding
sentences.text: Professor of International Law and Dutch politicians for the Labour Party, Nico Schrijver considered Rosenthal's threat to cut government funding if ICCO continues its financial support to The Electronic Intifada as very worrying.

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: Daoud Kuttab described EI as a pro-Palestinian website and part of the new media in the Arab world.

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: According to Foreign Policy, EI was a site that encouraged media activism and was part of the pro-Palestine camp of the Middle East conflict's cyberfront, opposite the pro-Israel Israel Support Group.

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: Gil Sedan, a Jewish Telegraphic Agency reporter in 2001, described EI as a "cyberpropaganda" site which "may contribute to a better understanding of the Palestinian cause," but also said that it "is too biased to be of much use to mainstream publications."

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: Hannah Brown of The Jerusalem Post in 2002 described EI as "one of the most elaborate" sites giving a "Palestinian perspective of the news".

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: According to Brown, EI is a "very professional, user-friendly and well written" website.

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: At this time, it included photographs "such as a picture of a lone, small Palestinian boy aiming a stone at an Israeli tank."

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: Political journalist Alexander Cockburn stated in The Nation in 2000: "there are a number of excellent news outlets for those who want unjaundiced reporting" describing The Electronic Intifada, and Middle East Research and Information Project, as "trustworthy".

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: NRC Handelsblad, a Dutch major mainstream newspaper, recommended The Electronic Intifada to its readers in 2006 at the height of the war on Lebanon.

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: NRC wrote, "The Electronic Intifada (EI), a news site in English, reports from a Palestinian perspective, but as impartial as possible.

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: EI is often faster than the established media."

sentences.section: Reception
sentences.text: In 2025, The Forward described EI's approach as emulating the pro-Israeli Committee for Accuracy in Middle East Reporting and Analysis (CAMERA).
